properties.areaDesc: Aransas Islands; Kleberg Islands; Nueces Islands; Calhoun Islands
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued October 9 at 11:56PM CDT until October 12 at 1:00AM CDT by NWS Corpus Christi TX
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents.
For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding.

* WHERE...Aransas Islands, Kleberg Islands, Nueces Islands and
Calhoun Islands Counties.

* WHEN...For the High Rip Current Risk, through Sunday morning.
For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 1 AM CDT Monday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of lots, parks, and roads with only
isolated road closures expected. Rip currents can sweep even
the most experienced swimmers away from shore into deeper
water. These rip currents can become life-threatening to
anyone entering the surf.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

properties.headline: Red Flag Warning issued October 9 at 9:53PM PDT until October 10 at 11:00PM PDT by NWS Elko NV
properties.description:
* Affected Area...Fire Weather Zone 424 Southeastern Humboldt
County and northern Lander County.

* WIND...Sustained winds up to 20-25 mph, gusts 35-40 mph.

* HUMIDITY...Humidity as low as 20-25% Saturday.

* Impacts...Any fires that develop will likely spread rapidly.
High winds may impact active wildfires to spread further.
Outdoor burning is not recommended. The combination of gusty
winds and low humidity will create critical fire weather
conditions.
properties.instruction:
A red flag warning means that critical fire weather conditions
are either occurring now, or will shortly. A combination of
strong winds, low relative humidity, and warm temperatures can
contribute to extreme fire behavior.

properties.instruction:
Thunderstorms can produce sudden waterspouts. Waterspouts can easily
overturn boats and create locally hazardous seas. Seek safe harbor
immediately. If your vessel is caught offshore, immediately secure
for heavy weather. Ensure all crew members are wearing USCG approved
Type I life jackets and nonessential crew are below decks. Deploy
jack lines and harnesses if available. Check life saving equipment,
including batteries on handheld radios, for readiness.

* WHEN...Until 1145 AM CDT Saturday.

and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring. Expect many

thunderstorms. Flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly
in the warned area. Between 7 and 12 inches of rain have fallen.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...

Springs, Sand Hill, Pleasant Ridge, Piney Grove, Fox Hill, Mossy

- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.
